newsitem.title: SYRIA: France's Chirac in Syria for talks with Assad.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac in Syria for talks with Assad.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac arrived in Damascus on Saturday at the start of a regional tour aimed at exerting efforts on stalled Arab-Israeli peace talks, officials said.

They said that President Hafez al-Assad and top Syrian officials welcomed Chirac at the airport. Thousands of Syrians also gathered there and lined up the road to the city to greet Chirac on his first visit to Syria as president.
Chirac and Assad will open talks at the presidential palace overlooking Damascus later in the day.
"France and Europe must stand by the parties as sources of friendship and proposals, and not as mere partners for reconstruction. It is time for Europe to co-sponsor this process as well," he said.

Chirac did not once mention the United States, the region's dominant power broker, which sidelined Europe in the talks. But he said there was a need to improve the framework and method of the negotiations, which had shown their limits in recent months.

Endorsing Syria's terms for resuming talks with Israel, he said peace was "only attainable on the basis of the achievements of the negotiations conducted for the last four years". Israel's hardline government has called for talks without preconditions, which Syria rejects as a return to square one.

Chirac said the essential principle of "land for peace" applied both to the Syrian Golan Heights, occupied by Israel since the 1967 Middle East war, and to Lebanon, where both Israel and Syria have troops.
